Id.fullDefinition: def Id (type : Type u) : Type u := type
Id.description: A type is defined that represents identity values for any given type.

Id.run.code: Id.run.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (x : Id α) : α
Id.run.fullDefinition: protected def run (x : Id α) : α := x
Id.run.description: A function is defined that retrieves the underlying value from an identity type for any given type.

Alternative.failure.code: Alternative.failure.{u, v} {f : Type u → Type v} [self : Alternative f] {α : Type u} : f α
Alternative.failure.comment:
Produces an empty collection or recoverable failure.  The `<|>` operator collects values or recovers
from failures. See `Alternative` for more details.
Alternative.failure.fullDefinition: failure : {α : Type u} → f α   /--   Depending on the `Alternative` instance, collects values or recovers from `failure`s by   returning the leftmost success. Can be written using the `<|>` operator syntax.   -/   orElse  : {α : Type u} → f α → (Unit → f α) → f α
Alternative.failure.description: A function is introduced that provides a mechanism to represent a failure or an empty collection in a context that supports alternatives.

guard.code: guard.{v} {f : Type → Type v} [Alternative f] (p : Prop) [Decidable p] : f Unit
guard.comment: If the proposition `p` is true, does nothing, else fails (using `failure`).
guard.fullDefinition: @[always_inline, inline] def guard {f : Type → Type v} [Alternative f] (p : Prop) [Decidable p] : f Unit :=   if p then pure () else failure
guard.description: A function is defined that checks a given proposition and performs no action if true, but results in a failure if false.

OptionT.run.code: OptionT.run.{u, v} {m : Type u → Type v} {α : Type u} (x : OptionT m α) : m (Option α)
OptionT.run.fullDefinition: def OptionT.run {m : Type u → Type v} {α : Type u} (x : OptionT m α) : m (Option α) :=   x
OptionT.run.description: A function is defined to execute an option transformer, resulting in a computation that yields an option within a monadic context.

OptionT.mk.code: OptionT.mk.{u, v} {m : Type u → Type v} {α : Type u} (x : m (Option α)) : OptionT m α
OptionT.mk.fullDefinition: protected def mk (x : m (Option α)) : OptionT m α :=   x
OptionT.mk.description: A function is defined to create an option transformer from a computation that produces an option.

LawfulMonad.mk'.code:
LawfulMonad.mk'.{u, v} (m : Type u → Type v) [Monad m] (id_map : ∀ {α : Type u} (x : m α), id <$> x = x)
  (pure_bind : ∀ {α β : Type u} (x : α) (f : α → m β), pure x >>= f = f x)
  (bind_assoc : ∀ {α β γ : Type u} (x : m α) (f : α → m β) (g : β → m γ), x >>= f >>= g = x >>= fun x => f x >>= g)
  (map_const : ∀ {α β : Type u} (x : α) (y : m β), Functor.mapConst x y = Function.const β x <$> y := by intros; rfl)
  (seqLeft_eq :
    ∀ {α β : Type u} (x : m α) (y : m β),
      (SeqLeft.seqLeft x fun x => y) = do
        let a ← x
        let _ ← y
        pure a := by
    intros; rfl)
  (seqRight_eq :
    ∀ {α β : Type u} (x : m α) (y : m β),
      (SeqRight.seqRight x fun x => y) = do
        let _ ← x
        y := by
    intros; rfl)
  (bind_pure_comp :
    ∀ {α β : Type u} (f : α → β) (x : m α),
      (do
          let y ← x
          pure (f y)) =
        f <$> x := by
    intros; rfl)
  (bind_map :
    ∀ {α β : Type u} (f : m (α → β)) (x : m α),
      (do
          let x_1 ← f
          x_1 <$> x) =
        Seq.seq f fun x_1 => x := by
    intros; rfl) :
  LawfulMonad m
LawfulMonad.mk'.comment:
An alternative constructor for `LawfulMonad` which has more
defaultable fields in the common case.
LawfulMonad.mk'.description: An alternative constructor for a lawful monad is provided, detailing how certain properties and behaviors of the monadic operations should relate to one another.

LawfulFunctor.comp_map.code:
LawfulFunctor.comp_map.{u, v} {f : Type u → Type v} [Functor f] [self : LawfulFunctor f] {α β γ : Type u} (g : α → β)
  (h : β → γ) (x : f α) : (h ∘ g) <$> x = h <$> g <$> x
LawfulFunctor.comp_map.description: The composition of two functions applied to a functor is shown to equal the functorial application of the individual functions applied sequentially to the functor.

LawfulFunctor.id_map.code:
LawfulFunctor.id_map.{u, v} {f : Type u → Type v} [Functor f] [self : LawfulFunctor f] {α : Type u} (x : f α) :
  id <$> x = x
LawfulFunctor.id_map.description: The identity function applied to a functor's value is demonstrated to be equivalent to the original value itself.

LawfulMonad.bind_pure_comp.code:
LawfulMonad.bind_pure_comp.{u, v} {m : Type u → Type v} [Monad m] [self : LawfulMonad m] {α β : Type u} (f : α → β)
  (x : m α) :
  (do
      let a ← x
      pure (f a)) =
    f <$> x
LawfulMonad.bind_pure_comp.description: The relationship between the monadic binding of a value followed by a pure function and the functorial application of that function to the value is established as being equivalent.

StateT.run_monadLift.code:
StateT.run_monadLift.{u, u_1, u_2} {m : Type u → Type u_1} {n : Type u → Type u_2} {α σ : Type u} [Monad m]
  [MonadLiftT n m] (x : n α) (s : σ) :
  (monadLift x).run s = do
    let a ← monadLift x
    pure (a, s)
StateT.run_monadLift.description: The behavior of lifting a monadic value in a stateful context is shown to result in a pair consisting of the lifted value and the original state.

ReaderT.run_monadLift.code:
ReaderT.run_monadLift.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {n : Type u_1 → Type u_2} {m : Type u_1 → Type u_3} {α ρ : Type u_1}
  [MonadLiftT n m] (x : n α) (ctx : ρ) : (monadLift x).run ctx = monadLift x
ReaderT.run_monadLift.description: The result shows that lifting a monadic value within a reader context returns the same lifted value when evaluated with a given context.

StateT.run_monadMap.code:
StateT.run_monadMap.{u, u_1, u_2} {m : Type u → Type u_1} {n : Type u → Type u_2} {σ α : Type u} [Monad m]
  [MonadFunctor n m] (f : {β : Type u} → n β → n β) (x : StateT σ m α) (s : σ) :
  (monadMap f x).run s = monadMap f (x.run s)
StateT.run_monadMap.description: The theorem demonstrates that mapping a function over a stateful monadic computation results in a computation that, when evaluated with the original state, behaves the same as applying the function to the result of the original computation.

ReaderT.run_monadMap.code:
ReaderT.run_monadMap.{u, u_1, u_2} {n : Type u → Type u_1} {m : Type u → Type u_2} {ρ α : Type u} [MonadFunctor n m]
  (f : {β : Type u} → n β → n β) (x : ReaderT ρ m α) (ctx : ρ) : (monadMap f x).run ctx = monadMap f (x.run ctx)
ReaderT.run_monadMap.description: The theorem establishes that applying a function to a reader monadic computation results in a computation that behaves the same when evaluated with a given context as if the function had been applied directly to the output of the original computation.

StateT.ext.code:
StateT.ext.{u_1, u_2} {σ : Type u_1} {m : Type u_1 → Type u_2} {α : Type u_1} {x y : StateT σ m α}
  (h : ∀ (s : σ), x.run s = y.run s) : x = y
StateT.ext.description: The theorem states that if two stateful computations yield the same result for every possible initial state, then the computations are considered equal.

ExceptT.ext.code:
ExceptT.ext.{u_1, u_2} {ε : Type u_1} {m : Type u_1 → Type u_2} {α : Type u_1} {x y : ExceptT ε m α}
  (h : x.run = y.run) : x = y
ExceptT.ext.description: The theorem asserts that if two computations in a contextual monad yield the same result, then the computations themselves are equal.

ReaderT.ext.code:
ReaderT.ext.{u_1, u_2} {ρ : Type u_1} {m : Type u_1 → Type u_2} {α : Type u_1} {x y : ReaderT ρ m α}
  (h : ∀ (ctx : ρ), x.run ctx = y.run ctx) : x = y
ReaderT.ext.description: The theorem asserts that if two reader computations produce the same result for every possible input context, then the computations are equal.

StateT.run_pure.code:
StateT.run_pure.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1 → Type u_2} {α σ : Type u_1} [Monad m] (a : α) (s : σ) :
  (pure a).run s = pure (a, s)
StateT.run_pure.description: The theorem demonstrates that running a pure monadic value in a stateful context results in a pair containing the value and the original state.

ExceptT.run_pure.code:
ExceptT.run_pure.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1 → Type u_2} {α ε : Type u_1} [Monad m] (x : α) :
  (pure x).run = pure (Except.ok x)
ExceptT.run_pure.description: The theorem establishes that running a pure value within a context produces a result that encapsulates the value as a successful outcome in the exception monad.

ReaderT.run_pure.code:
ReaderT.run_pure.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1 → Type u_2} {α ρ : Type u_1} [Monad m] (a : α) (ctx : ρ) :
  (pure a).run ctx = pure a
ReaderT.run_pure.description: The theorem demonstrates that running a pure value within a reader context yields the same pure value when evaluated with any context.

StateT.run_bind.code:
StateT.run_bind.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1 → Type u_2} {σ α β : Type u_1} [Monad m] (x : StateT σ m α)
  (f : α → StateT σ m β) (s : σ) :
  (x >>= f).run s = do
    let p ← x.run s
    (f p.fst).run p.snd
StateT.run_bind.description: The theorem demonstrates how binding a stateful computation to a function results in a new computation that processes both the state and the output of the initial computation appropriately.

ExceptT.run_bind.code:
ExceptT.run_bind.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1 → Type u_2} {ε α β : Type u_1} {f : α → ExceptT ε m β} [Monad m]
  (x : ExceptT ε m α) :
  (x >>= f).run = do
    let x ← x.run
    match x with
      | Except.ok x => (f x).run
      | Except.error e => pure (Except.error e)
ExceptT.run_bind.description: The theorem demonstrates how binding an exception monadic value to a function yields a result that either continues with the function's outcome if successful or returns an error if the initial value was an error.

ReaderT.run_bind.code:
ReaderT.run_bind.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1 → Type u_2} {ρ α β : Type u_1} [Monad m] (x : ReaderT ρ m α)
  (f : α → ReaderT ρ m β) (ctx : ρ) :
  (x >>= f).run ctx = do
    let a ← x.run ctx
    (f a).run ctx
ReaderT.run_bind.description: The theorem establishes that binding a reader monadic value to a function results in the execution of the original value followed by applying the function to the obtained result, both in the context of a given environment.

StateT.run_map.code:
StateT.run_map.{u, u_1} {m : Type u → Type u_1} {α β σ : Type u} [Monad m] [LawfulMonad m] (f : α → β)
  (x : StateT σ m α) (s : σ) : (f <$> x).run s = (fun p => (f p.fst, p.snd)) <$> x.run s
StateT.run_map.description: The theorem establishes that mapping a function over a stateful computation yields the same result as applying the function to the output of the computation while keeping the state unchanged.

ExceptT.run_map.code:
ExceptT.run_map.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1 → Type u_2} {α β ε : Type u_1} [Monad m] [LawfulMonad m] (f : α → β)
  (x : ExceptT ε m α) : (f <$> x).run = Except.map f <$> x.run
ExceptT.run_map.description: The theorem shows that mapping a function over a computation that might fail results in a computation that applies the function to successful outcomes while preserving the failure structure.

ReaderT.run_map.code:
ReaderT.run_map.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1 → Type u_2} {α β ρ : Type u_1} [Monad m] (f : α → β) (x : ReaderT ρ m α)
  (ctx : ρ) : (f <$> x).run ctx = f <$> x.run ctx
ReaderT.run_map.description: The theorem demonstrates that mapping a function over a reader monadic value yields the same result as applying the function to the output of the value when evaluated in a specific context.

StateT.code: StateT.{u, v} (σ : Type u) (m : Type u → Type v) (α : Type u) : Type (max u v)
StateT.fullDefinition: def StateT (σ : Type u) (m : Type u → Type v) (α : Type u) : Type (max u v) :=   σ → m (α × σ)
StateT.description: A type is defined that encapsulates stateful computations transforming a given state type and an effectful computation type into a new type.

StateT.run.code: StateT.run.{u, v} {σ : Type u} {m : Type u → Type v} {α : Type u} (x : StateT σ m α) (s : σ) : m (α × σ)
StateT.run.fullDefinition: def StateT.run {σ : Type u} {m : Type u → Type v} {α : Type u} (x : StateT σ m α) (s : σ) : m (α × σ) :=   x s
StateT.run.description: A function is defined that executes a stateful computation by providing it with an initial state, producing a result along with the updated state.

ExceptT.mk.code: ExceptT.mk.{u, v} {ε : Type u} {m : Type u → Type v} {α : Type u} (x : m (Except ε α)) : ExceptT ε m α
ExceptT.mk.fullDefinition: def ExceptT.mk {ε : Type u} {m : Type u → Type v} {α : Type u} (x : m (Except ε α)) : ExceptT ε m α := x
ExceptT.mk.description: A function is defined to create an exception transformer from a computation that yields either a value or an error.

ExceptT.run.code: ExceptT.run.{u, v} {ε : Type u} {m : Type u → Type v} {α : Type u} (x : ExceptT ε m α) : m (Except ε α)
ExceptT.run.fullDefinition: def ExceptT.run {ε : Type u} {m : Type u → Type v} {α : Type u} (x : ExceptT ε m α) : m (Except ε α) := x
ExceptT.run.description: A function is defined to execute an exception transformer and return a computation that may produce either a value or an error.

StateRefT'.run.code:
StateRefT'.run {ω σ : Type} {m : Type → Type} [Monad m] [MonadLiftT (ST ω) m] {α : Type} (x : StateRefT' ω σ m α)
  (s : σ) : m (α × σ)
StateRefT'.run.fullDefinition: def StateRefT'.run {ω σ : Type} {m : Type → Type} [Monad m] [MonadLiftT (ST ω) m] {α : Type} (x : StateRefT' ω σ m α) (s : σ) : m (α × σ) := do   let ref ← ST.mkRef s   let a ← x ref   let s ← ref.get   pure (a, s)
StateRefT'.run.description: A function is defined to execute a stateful computation within a monadic context, producing a result along with an updated state.
